title: Links between SDG 3 and other goals
log: 2026-11-01T14:46:38Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new
2026-11-02T04:41:50Z recheck: the fresh check agreed with the fix, cleared with the fix

match.reason: The closest bank point covers links between health and only goals 1, 4 and 6, not goals 2, 5 and 12, and its questions test the definition of Goal 3 rather than the links the new point teaches, so it is narrower than the brief.

draft.title: Links between SDG 3 and other goals
card: The goals are connected. Progress on SDG 3 depends on progress on other goals, because many causes of poor health lie outside health care.
SDG 1 and 2
Ending poverty and hunger. People with enough income and food can afford care, and are less likely to be undernourished or to get sick.
SDG 4 and 5
Quality education and gender equality. Education helps people understand and act on health information. Equality helps girls and women reach health care and make choices about their health.
SDG 6 and 12
Clean water and sanitation, and responsible consumption. Safe water and sanitation prevent many infections, and less pollution and waste reduces harm to health.
draft.remember: Health depends on more than health care: poverty, food, education, equality, water and consumption all play a part.

a.q: Why does progress on SDG 6 (clean water and sanitation) help to achieve SDG 3?
opts: Safe water and sanitation prevent many infections
Clean water gives girls the same chances as boys
Safe water means people no longer need any health care
Clean water raises household income through school fees
a.why: Safe water and sanitation prevent infections that cause illness and death, which supports SDG 3. It does not remove the need for health care, so the option claiming that is wrong.
a.clue: Think about what unsafe water can spread.

b.q: In a rural region, many girls leave school early and few women can make decisions about seeing a doctor. Which two goals would most help improve health there?
opts: SDG 4 and SDG 5
SDG 1 and SDG 6
SDG 2 and SDG 12
SDG 6 and SDG 12
b.why: Girls leaving school is an education issue (SDG 4), and women's limited say over their health care is a gender equality issue (SDG 5). Poverty and water matter for health too, but the scenario does not describe them.
b.clue: Match the problems in the scenario to education and equality.

a.best: Safe water and sanitation prevent many infections

problems.detail: The clue 'Match the problems in the scenario to education and equality' names the two goals (education = SDG 4, gender equality = SDG 5), so it gives away the answer instead of prompting thinking.
